title: pool-performance-interference-synthesis-and-immediate-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note synthesizes the observations from the Nov 4–6 GPU pool performance degradation window, proposes a concise immediate-response playbook for on-call, and lists medium-term mitigations to prevent noisy-neighbor and autoscaler misconfiguration issues.

Scope / WHY this doc exists:
- Dedicated-capacity pools serving Dedicated customers experienced intermittent latency spikes and token-rate tail latencies between 11/04 22:00 UTC and 11/06 07:30 UTC.
- Impact profile: 3 customers reported >=2x P95 latency regressions; no data exfiltration or SLA breach recorded yet.
- Primary hypotheses: (1) high-throughput single-tenant jobs saturating GPU SM/PCIe (noisy neighbor), (2) autoscaler misconfig allowed aggressive packing without respecting MIG/instance isolation, (3) background system-level jobs (snapshotting, NVRAM scrubbing) overlapping with peak requests.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause likely multi-factor: long-running inference jobs with pathological batch sizes + autoscaler packing rules that disabled isolation led to high sustained GPU SM utilization and KV-cache thrash. A subset of hosts also had intermittent driver-level thermal throttling (older driver) that amplified tail latencies.
- Immediate mitigations (applied during the outage): throttle configured auto-burst for suspect tenants, cordon+drain of 4 affected nodes, roll forward of a small kernel driver rollback on 2 nodes.
- Next steps: enforce placement policies (soft taints for burst workloads), add telemetry for per-tenant SM utilization, and update autoscaler policy to avoid colocating >2 high-throughput pods per GPU.

Observed signals and quick data pulls used in triage:
- p95/p99 latency graphs (per-pool) from telemetry dashboard (console -> pool/compute -> latency) showing correlated spikes with increase in GPU_util_pct.
- DCGM counters: SM_util, memory_copy_util, sm_avg_power_watts, gpu_temperature_celsius.
- nvidia-smi pmon logs on impacted hosts showing persistent 98–100% SM utilization across multiple processes.
- kube-metrics-server and cAdvisor: container_cpu and container_memory not a signal; GPU metrics are required for meaningful isolation.
- Autoscaler logs: scale decisions at 2025-11-05T03:12:21Z showed two compacting decisions that placed 3 high-throughput pods onto a single multi-GPU host.

Short timeline (UTC):
- 2025-11-04 21:45 — First alert: pool latency P95 jump (automated threshold).
- 2025-11-04 21:50 — On-call (Asha) acknowledges; begins data pull, opens JIRA-ENG-7821.
- 2025-11-04 22:10 — Slack channel #sre-dedicated-capacity created; 2 customers flagged.
- 2025-11-05 02:58 — Autoscaler executed packing decision after scale-down window; 3 large inference tasks placed together.
- 2025-11-05 03:06 — nvidia-smi pmon capture shows multiple processes at SM 96–100%.
- 2025-11-05 03:22 — Temporary mitigation: bump per-tenant QPS limit and trigger slow-start backoff.
- 2025-11-05 03:40 — Team cordoned 4 nodes suspected of contributing; traffic draining initiated.
- 2025-11-05 04:15 — Driver rollback applied to 2 hosts that exhibited thermal throttling; tail latency improved.
- 2025-11-06 07:35 — All pools returned to baseline; incident moved to post-incident review.

Immediate-response playbook (concise checklist for on-call):
1) Alert handling and data collection (first 15 min):
   - Acknowledge incident, create ticket (JIRA ticket if not already), bump paging channel.
   - Query per-pool GPU telemetry: SM_util, mem_util, decoder/encoder stalls, temperature. Use prebuilt graphite/grafana dashboard query: pool.cpu.gpu_sm_pct, pool.dcgm.memcopy, pool.p95_latency.
   - Take pmon snapshot on top-affected nodes: ssh node -> sudo nvidia-smi pmon -s u -i <gpu_index> > /tmp/pmon-<node>-<ts>.log.
   - Export recent autoscaler decision log window (±30m).
2) Immediate mitigations (first 15–60 min):
   - If persistent SM_util >90% across >2 GPUs on a single host, mark node as noisy: kubectl label node <node> redwood/noisy=true (temporary marker).
   - For noisy nodes: cordon + drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-local-data, then shift customer traffic away.
   - Throttle suspect tenants by setting per-tenant QPS ceiling via edge-config (console -> tenants -> throttle) to reduce burst patterns.
   - If autoscaler placed >2 high-throughput pods per GPU, manually scale up pool to relieve packing pressure: update pool replica count and annotate autoscaler with override=manual-pause.
   - If driver/thermal suspicious signs present: reduce clock via nvidia-smi --applications-clocks or restart nvidia driver (sudo systemctl restart nvidia-drm) on affected host after drain.
3) Validation:
   - Watch latency and SM_util converge; require p95 drop to baseline for 30m before uncordoning.
4) Communications:
   - Post status updates to #sre-dedicated-capacity every 30 minutes and to CS/customer success for affected tenants.

Runbook additions (drafted for inclusion into the main SRE runbook):
- Add per-tenant SM utilization metric ingestion into the long-term metrics store (reduce sampling to 10s on suspect tenants only).
- Autoscaler policy changes: disallow packing more than N_high_throughput_pods=2 per host; use a scoring function that penalizes sustained SM_util > 75% for last 5m.
- Define tenant profile labels: bursty, sustained-heavy, low. Use these to guide placement.
- Add a node marker and lifecycle: redwood/noisy with TTL annotation set by on-call who cordoned the node (so it auto-expires in 6h unless escalated).
- Prebaked scripts: /opt/redwood/sre/bin/collect-gpu-snapshot.sh and /opt/redwood/sre/bin/soft-throttle-tenant.sh (TODO: add to repo and sign with SRE key).

Investigation notes (what we think happened):
- The autoscaler aggressive compaction policy (pack-to-util) considered only GPU memory footprint and not SM utilization. Two things coincided: a customer started several multi-stream high-QPS pods (inference server with large batch window) and autoscaler placed them together to avoid idle memory; the resulting SM saturation caused long tail latency.
- Aged driver on two nodes manifested as thermal throttling when SM_util was near-100%, amplifying latency spikes.
- No evidence of malicious or noisy scanner (no cron jobs or snapshots scheduled in logs), but system-level background GC jobs overlapped on one node.

Data & ad-hoc queries used (for reference):
- Grafana query snippets: max_over_time(pool_gpu_sm_pct[5m]) by (node,pool)
- DCGM scraping: curl http://dcgm-exporter:9100/metrics | grep -E 'dcgm_gpu_sm_clock|dcgm_gpu_util'
- Kubernetes: kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> -o wide | xargs -I {} kubectl top pod {} --containers
- ssh checks: sudo nvidia-smi -q -d UTILIZATION,TEMPERATURE,POWER > /tmp/gpu_q_<ts>.txt

Short-term remediation plan (owner + ETA):
- (Asha) Update playbook checklist into SRE runbook and deploy prebaked scripts — ETA 2025-11-12.
- (Liam) Autoscaler policy PR to include SM_util heuristics and max-colocate limit — PR and config change by 2025-11-18 (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/439).
- (Maya) Add per-tenant SM telemetry ingestion and dashboard — ETA 2025-11-21.
- (Samir) Node marker TTL automation: Kubernetes operator to expire redwood/noisy after 6h unless SRE extends — ETA 2025-12-02.

Longer-term mitigations and wishlist:
- Per-tenant admission control on bursty workloads (token-bucket based) at the edge that feeds back into placement decisions.
- GPU-level QoS primitives (NVIDIA MIG-based enforcement, or cgroups v2 + gpu-isolator) — research spike requested.
- Firmware/driver upgrade sweep for all pools to remove thermal regression vectors.
- Autoscaler integration test harness that simulates bursty tenants and validates no >2 high-throughput pods colocated.

Open questions (for follow-up):
- What is the acceptable tradeoff between packing efficiency and latency SLO for Dedicated customers? (product to weigh in)
- Should we automatically throttle tenants above a sustained SM_util threshold even if they paid for dedicated capacity? (policy + commercial implications)
- Do we need a preemptive warm-node pool for bursty jobs?

Post-incident actions & owners (concrete):
- Create config flag: autoscaler.max_colocate_highqps = 2 (Liam) — JIRA-ENG-7894.
- Add SM_util to tenant billing telemetry for transparency (Maya) — JIRA-ENG-7896.
- Run driver/firmware upgrade planning across Dedicated fleets (Infra lead) — JIRA-ENG-7902.
- Customer outreach: CS to notify affected customers with root-cause summary and mitigation timeline (Evelyn) — Outreach ticket CS-4301.

Notes to on-call (less formal):
- When in doubt, cordon+drain noisy nodes early — don’t wait for perfect evidence. The human cost of chasing low-fidelity signals is higher than quickly relieving packing pressure.
- Keep communications tight: one person owns status updates to customers.
- If you suspect driver-level issues, prefer rolling-restart of driver after drain rather than rebooting host in-place unless instructed.

Appendix: quick commands list (copy/paste friendly)
- Collect pmon: ssh node && sudo nvidia-smi pmon -c 1 > /tmp/pmon-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%s).log
- Label node noisy: kubectl label node <node> redwood/noisy=true --overwrite
- Cordon + drain: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>
- Throttle tenant via edge (example CLI): redwood edge throttle set --tenant <tenant-id> --qps 150

End of draft.

Comments / edits welcome — this should be a short, practical playbook for first responders and a basis for the runbook PR.
